pillar_reactions.evidence: Engaged on mechanics rather than benefits, and asked the one question that matters to someone who has hurt himself teaching himself before: 'What do you guys do to help enable someone to be able to dial in the form right from the get-go? Do you have a library of videos or something that somebody can watch?' Accepted the answer — a video library plus form videos reviewed by the coach — with 'Yes. Perfect.'

Declined the pillar twice before it was delivered and once during. When the rep asked him to walk through a normal day he cut it off: 'I'm really looking for help with the programming on the workouts. The diet and nutrition, I'm probably pretty good on.' And when asked whether the weight loss might be a diet problem: 'I'm pretty sure it's the programming and the consistency there.' Roughly a third of what he would be paying for is something he has explicitly said he does not want.

Presented as the coach's personal number, weekly check-in forms, programme adjustments and chasing when workouts are not logged. Understood and agreed without questions or enthusiasm — 'Okay. You get an accountability thing. Okay.'

anchors.raw: Why was I told that it was between two and four? By who? I got it in the text message thread.
anchors.note: The company's own automated texting anchored him at $2,000-$4,000 before the call. He raised it as a process complaint, not a haggle — 'Whoever's answering those texts, you might want to have them not set expectations with people that way' — which means the anchor cost trust as well as price room.

anchors.raw: we also have on the lower end. So we have a do it yourself way that is 2k per year and a three months that is 4k
anchors.note: Disclosed live to resolve the mismatch. It gave a comparison shopper who had already said he mainly wants programming two cheaper Primal options to weigh against the recommended one, and his read was immediate: 'So there were other options available. You just went right at the six. I get it.'

anchors.raw: As far as the program itself goes, I mean, it's pretty much par for the course. Everybody's in that $4,000 $6,000 range.
anchors.note: He has already priced the category and placed Primal at the top of the band with nothing distinguishing it. This is the sharpest positioning signal in the batch: an on-ICP buyer with no affordability constraint saying the offer is undifferentiated at the ceiling of the market.

anchors.raw: I've got four of these calls scheduled, and I'm considering one more, and I'm trying to understand what the differences in the programs are.
anchors.note: A structured evaluation with a decision date, not a browse. The one competitor already seen lost on manner rather than substance — 'they were very condescending with me... they took a very elitist kind of approach' — which was a free brief on how to win him, and it was acknowledged and dropped.

unmet_demand.want: A clear statement of what Primal does differently from the four other providers he is evaluating
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Asked three times — 'I wanted to have this call to understand what's different about what you guys do from the others that are out there' — and answered each time with the standard three-pillar walkthrough. He left rating the offer as par for the course.

unmet_demand.want: Programming and coaching without the nutrition component, which he says he does not need
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer is priced and delivered as three bundled pillars. The rep verbally de-emphasised nutrition — 'I will communicate to him, then that's not your biggest goal point' — but nothing in the price or structure changed, so he is being asked to pay full freight for a third he has declined.

unmet_demand.want: To start immediately, while travelling for the next two weeks
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He said yes to starting during the travel — 'is it actually something you would want to start with during the travels already?' → 'Yes' — and it was never converted into anything. No onboarding call, no deposit, no start date, despite him separately saying 'I actually want to get started sooner.'
